title: Retire AI/ML-era passage scoring; extend for threat-intel report structure
description:
Retire passage-scoring heuristics that were tuned for a previous AI/ML-research corpus and extend them for threat-intel report structure. Small, self-contained, zero dependencies — a good calibration assignment.

## Current state (verified 2026-07-19)

- `PASSAGE_HEADING_BOOSTS` (`src/papyrus_knowledge_query/engine.py:43-51`): boosts only academic headings (abstract 8, introduction 4, evaluation 5, results 5, findings 5, discussion 3, conclusion 3).
- `_passage_score` (`engine.py:2994-3013`): hardcoded penalties for "uc berkeley", "ibm research", "correspondence to:", "project co-leads" (line 2999); hardcoded +2 boost for tokens {"reliability", "evaluation", "production", "agents", "practitioners"} (line 3011). These overfit one prior corpus.
- `_keywords` (`engine.py:3016-3021`): regex `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,}` drops digit-leading tokens (many hashes), and splits dotted domains and IP addresses.
- `_looks_like_heading` (`engine.py:2985-2991`) treats membership in PASSAGE_HEADING_BOOSTS as heading evidence — new keys must be lowercase.

## Design decisions (current thinking — challenge them if you have better information)

1. **EXTEND the heading boosts, don't replace them.** This instance also ingests academic AI/ML papers (see `docs/automation-ai-ml-academic-research-dispatch.md` — corpus `AI-ML-research`), so academic headings stay. ADD threat-intel report headings, all lowercase keys: `executive summary: 8`, `key judgments: 6`, `iocs: 6`, `indicators of compromise: 6`, `attribution: 5`, `detections: 5`, `detection opportunities: 5`, `technical analysis: 4`, `mitigations: 4`, `recommendations: 4`, `timeline: 3`.
2. **Delete the corpus-specific token boost line** (`engine.py:3011`, the reliability/evaluation/agents/practitioners set) entirely. Keyword overlap already does that work. Do NOT replace with threat-intel terms — that would repeat the same mistake.
3. **Replace the named-org penalties** (line 2999) with generic boilerplate markers: `"about the author"`, `"copyright ©"`, `"subscribe to"`, `"newsletter"`, `"all rights reserved"`. Keep the references/bibliography and URL-density penalties — those are corpus-neutral.
4. **Fix the token regex** in `_keywords` to `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{2,}` so digit-leading hashes and dotted domains/IPs survive as tokens. Do NOT touch `keyword_set` in `ranking.py` — it has separate consumers (`lexical_relevance`) and separate tests; changing both at once muddies attribution if behavior shifts.

## Files to modify

- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/engine.py` — the three items above.
- `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_knowledge_query.py` — add tests: (a) a passage under an "Executive Summary" heading outscores an equivalent passage under no heading; (b) `_keywords` captures `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`, `example.com`, `192.0.2.1` as single tokens; (c) academic headings still boost (regression guard).

## What could go wrong

- **Existing tests may snapshot current scores.** Run the suite first (`pytest procedures/newsroom/tests/test_knowledge_query.py`), understand failures before changing expectations.
- **The regex change widens token sets**, which slightly changes keyword-overlap scores everywhere `_keywords` is used (passage selection). This is intended, but check that passage selection on existing fixtures still picks sensible passages.
- **Heading keys must be lowercase** and ≤90 chars or `_looks_like_heading` won't match them.

## Out of scope

Any lexical index, BM25, or fusion work (separate epic). Any change to `ranking.py`.
